knowledge.title: Ransomware triage
knowledge.text: Preserve the note, file samples, process history and authentication records. Verify modification content and backup integrity. Escalate active destructive behavior for containment approval.

knowledge.title: File service containment
knowledge.text: Coordinate with the service owner before isolating a file server. Identify connected clients, account scope, backup isolation and business impact.

knowledge.title: Vulnerability triage
knowledge.text: Match ecosystem, package and installed version. Validate reachability and exploit prerequisites. A matching advisory does not identify the cause of an incident.

stages.title: Critical alert
stages.why: The detection queue supplies a critical host alert. An arrival event starts the automation.
stages.output: One scoped alert, ready for admission checks.

stages.title: Validate & queue
stages.why: Application code validates scope and rejects duplicate deliveries before starting an investigation.

stages.title: Review related alerts
stages.why: The AI asks for context; a scoped MCP adapter reads related events from Wazuh.

stages.title: Retrieve runbooks
stages.why: RAG supplies response guidance and operational constraints, with versioned citations.

stages.title: Inspect evidence
stages.why: The model chooses focused checks; tool adapters return bounded evidence and explicit limitations.
stages.output: E3–E9 · process ancestry, artifact, inventory and network context

stages.title: Cross-reference intelligence
stages.why: Query MISP, inspect source reports, and check package exposure without inventing an exploit chain.
stages.output: Intelligence reports + OSV advisory matches · exposure is not exploitation

stages.title: Build assessment
stages.why: The AI combines evidence, guidance and tool limits into a decision the analyst can review.
stages.output: Prioritized assessment with evidence and action owners

stages.title: Analyst review
stages.why: The automation creates a reviewable handoff, then waits for the analyst’s decision.

assessment.title: Suspected ransomware activity on FILESVR-01
assessment.confidence: High triage urgency · Moderate confidence in ransomware hypothesis
assessment.summary: A Qilin-labelled DLL hash match, a ransom-note write, a burst of Finance-share file modifications, and a shadow-copy deletion command warrant urgent incident response. The supplied records do not yet prove encryption, successful backup deletion, or activity on a second server.

findings.title: Possible destructive activity
findings.text: The note and modification burst coincide on FILESVR-01. Inspect before/after file samples to distinguish encryption from legitimate bulk changes.

findings.title: Execution history needs preservation
findings.text: An empty process snapshot does not clear earlier execution. Preserve script, logon-session mapping and command outcome.

findings.title: Known file hash raises triage priority
findings.text: The collected DLL hash matches a Qilin-labelled public record; prioritize file provenance and loader telemetry. Execution remains unverified.

findings.title: Separate vulnerability exposure
findings.text: Jinja2 3.1.4 matches public advisories on both reporting servers. Nothing in this evidence links template rendering to the file modifications.

actions.action: Confirm whether writes are still occurring. If destructive activity continues, approve containment after assessing dependents.
Preserve the note and representative modified files; collect process ancestry and security logs for 16:30–16:50 UTC.
Preserve recovery.dll and verify hash provenance before attributing changes to Qilin.
Verify offline or immutable recovery points. The shadow-copy command alone does not establish deletion success.

limitations: File-content comparison, command exit status, and process attribution for the blocked request remain missing.
A prior exercise used the note template; current exercise approval remains unverified.
